chunks: That is indicated by what the Shaykh—may Allah Most High support him—informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about tayammum,

He said: “'Ammar was affected by janabah, so he rolled about as an animal rolls about. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him, while mocking him: ‘O 'Ammar, you rolled about as an animal rolls about.’”
So we said to him: Then how is tayammum? He placed his two hands upon the ground, then raised them, and wiped his face and his hands a little above the wrists.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum, dry ablution performed with earth or dust in place of wudu or ghusl
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth or ground used for tayammum
key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: his face, one of the areas wiped in tayammum
key_terms.يَدَيْهِ: his two hands, which are wiped in tayammum

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام about 'Ammar?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of tayammum through the teaching of Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام and by recalling the incident of 'Ammar. It shows that tayammum is performed by striking or placing the hands on the earth and wiping the face and hands, rather than rolling the body in dust. The report is significant in jurisprudence for describing the practical form of ritual purification when water is unavailable or unusable.
